title: Ivo and the Harvest
premise: Ulyana Delacroix, a skeptical urban explorer, discovers unmapped tunnels beneath the derelict Harrow House and takes a small brass key as a souvenir. The house begins claiming them: mirrors lag one second behind reality, then begin showing rooms that don't exist, then showing Ulyana things they did in 1974—a year they weren't alive. The tunnels belong to the Harvest, an entity fed by the town's founding families, who in 1974 sacrificed a child named Ivo to seal their bargain; Ulyana's grandmother was one of them. To survive, Ulyana must return what was taken—both the key and the truth of Ivo's name, erased from every record—and confront the surviving conspirators before the Harvest collects its overdue debt. In the end Ulyana gives back the key and speaks Ivo's name aloud in the deepest tunnel, freeing his ghost but binding themselves as the Harvest's new witness: they walk out changed, remembering everything, unable to ever disbelieve again.
about_author: Vesper Yarrow is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing sealed municipal records in upstate New York. They write horror about paperwork, places, and the debts towns prefer to forget.

chapters.title: The Survey That Isn't
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. An urban explorer with a rule against believing anything they can't photograph, Ulyana breaks into Harrow House to map tunnels missing from every survey. They find a brass key on a ribbon labeled with a date: 1974. Emotional beat: confident curiosity curdling into unease when their own flashlight beam seems to arrive late.

chapters.title: One Second Behind
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Back home, every mirror reflects the room a full second late. Ulyana tests it obsessively—timers, phone cameras—but the lag only grows. Their skepticism becomes a coping mechanism. Emotional beat: rational denial stretched thin over creeping dread.

chapters.title: Rooms Without Doors
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The mirrors begin showing rooms that don't exist in their apartment: a nursery, a kitchen with a pot boiling on a dead stove. A figure stands in one, facing away. Ulyana photographs everything; the photos show only empty glass. Emotional beat: isolation, the first sense of being watched rather than haunted.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV, with interleaved ledger excerpts. Sorting their late grandmother Odile Delacroix's estate, Ulyana finds a household ledger from 1974 with pages razored out and the word HARVEST written in a child's hand inside the cover. Emotional beat: grief for the grandmother colliding with the first crack of belief.

chapters.title: The Town That Forgot a Boy
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Research reveals no record of any child named Ivo in the county—not births, not deaths, not missing persons. Yet the ledger's handwriting matches a boy's schoolwork Odile kept hidden. Someone was deliberately erased. Emotional beat: the horror of bureaucratic absence, loyalty to family memory beginning to war with truth.

chapters.title: Return to Harrow House
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. They go back at night with the key. The tunnels are longer than they mapped; doors now stand where there were none. A voice repeats their name in their grandmother's cadence. Ulyana flees but leaves the key behind by accident—or so they think. Emotional beat: panic, loss of control.

chapters.title: What Mirrors Remember
chapters.summary: POV shifts to the mirrors themselves—an uncanny second-person interlude describing what the glass has witnessed since 1974: six adults, one child, a promise kept in the dark. Emotional beat: dread deepened by intimacy; the house has been waiting patiently.

chapters.title: The Survivors
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Three of the 1974 conspirators are still alive. Ulyana tracks down Ruth Ambrose, ninety-one and lucid, who slams the door after saying only: 'We paid. We paid in full.' Emotional beat: confrontation denied; power protecting itself with silence.

chapters.title: Ruth's Confession, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. A second visit; Ruth, terrified by the mirrors in her own home lagging now too, begins confessing—the founding families' bargain, the annual tithe, the final payment in '74—when her son arrives and cuts her off, threatening Ulyana. Emotional beat: truth almost surfacing, smothered by inherited complicity.

chapters.title: The Second Believer
chapters.summary: POV of Marcus Hale, another conspirator's descendant, a local historian who has spent years quietly documenting anomalies he refuses to name. He contacts Ulyana after finding their exploration posts. Emotional beat: wary alliance; two skeptics discovering they were never alone.

chapters.title: Down Where the Years Pool
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Marcus explore the tunnels together with instruments. Time behaves badly down there—watches disagree, a match burns backward. They find a small room with children's chalk drawings and one name scratched over and over: IVO. Emotional beat: awe and terror; the past is physically present.

chapters.title: Odile's Tape
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Hidden in the ledger's spine, a cassette: Odile's voice, recorded in 1974, confessing her part and begging forgiveness from a boy who cannot hear it. She calls him 'our Ivo.' Ulyana listens alone, weeping. Emotional beat: grief and fury; loyalty to the grandmother now inseparable from betrayal by her.

chapters.title: The Lag Spreads
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Across town, mirrors lag everywhere—storefronts, car rearviews, the police station. People report seeing 'someone standing just behind you, patient.' The Harvest is collecting attention, not just souls. Emotional beat: escalating communal dread; secrecy collapsing.

chapters.title: Power's Price
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. He reveals his family kept the bargain's terms: the Harvest grants the town prosperity in exchange for being fed memory—each generation forgetting a little more, the erasure of Ivo the largest withdrawal. Power corrupts because it is literally purchased with other people's existence. Emotional beat: bitter clarity.

chapters.title: They Come for Ruth
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Rushing to protect Ruth, Ulyana finds her home dark, every mirror shattered, Ruth gone—taken as the overdue interest on 1974. Her son blames Ulyana. Emotional beat: guilt, failure, the cost of arriving late to old crimes.

chapters.title: The Terms of Return
chapters.summary: Ulyana and Marcus decode the ledger's remaining pages: the debt can be discharged only by returning what was taken—the key, the name, and a living witness who chooses to remember. Not sacrifice: witness. The Harvest feeds on forgetting; remembrance starves it. Emotional beat: grim hope, a plan with a terrible personal cost.

chapters.title: Everything We Buried
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. Preparations: restoring Ivo's name to records, calling the remaining descendants, publishing Odile's tape. Some descendants beg them to stop; one tries to burn the ledger. Ulyana realizes how many people profit from not knowing. Emotional beat: defiance hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Ulyana descends alone—Marcus stays above as the second witness, the ritual requiring two: one to remember below, one to speak above. The tunnels rearrange around them, offering exits, bargains, their grandmother's voice. Emotional beat: loneliness at maximum depth, temptation to turn back.

chapters.title: Ivo
chapters.summary: Climax, Ulyana's POV. In the chalk room, Ulyana meets what remains of Ivo—not a monster but a nine-year-old frozen mid-fear, sustained by the Harvest as both meal and jailer. Ulyana returns the key, speaks his full reconstructed name, and describes him aloud in detail, giving him back his existence. The Harvest convulses as fifty years of enforced forgetting reverses. Emotional beat: compassion as weapon; the moment disbelief dies forever.

chapters.title: Above Ground
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. As Ulyana remembers below, Marcus reads names and dates aloud at the tunnel mouth while the town's mirrors shudder and clear. Ivo's records restore themselves in archives across the county. Ruth Ambrose walks out of the fog, aged but alive, remembering everything she paid away. Emotional beat: release, exhaustion, dawn.

chapters.title: The New Witness
chapters.summary: Ulyana's POV. The price of witnessing: Ulyana can never again not-believe. Every reflection shows true; every forgotten thing in the town surfaces in their memory whether they want it or not. They take up Odile's ledger and begin writing the town's real history. Emotional beat: bittersweet acceptance of a burden chosen freely.

chapters.title: Harvest Season
chapters.summary: Epilogue, mixed POV. One year later: the town prospers still, but now it knows why, and holds an unnamed memorial each autumn. In the last mirror scene, the lag is gone—except once, briefly, a boy's hand waves from the glass, not trapped anymore, just saying goodbye. Final line lands on Ulyana waving back. Emotional beat: mourning transmuted into vigilance; memory as ongoing labor.
